### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **210** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/stored-reference-package-backfill.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**48** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/stored-reference-package-backfill.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **20** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **48** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f6b7146872a03e8e96b86570d74e6ea6995a6544` — the merge of head `e714e9b92994022853ec1176873d5ae9d88ccbbb` into base `45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f6b7146872a03e8e96b86570d74e6ea6995a6544 && git checkout f6b7146872a03e8e96b86570d74e6ea6995a6544
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16 e714e9b92994022853ec1176873d5ae9d88ccbbb && git checkout -B drift-repro 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16 && git merge --no-ff e714e9b92994022853ec1176873d5ae9d88ccbbb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Epic red-line review of #32091 (#31696 PR-1, `Part of #31696`) at head 77fa2e35: PASS.** It lands once CI is green and the seat ACCEPTs.

- **Red line 1, never loosen: holds.**
  - **The sealed clash.** It moves from "arming neither" to "each package's flow in its own slot". That is not a looser resolution. Nothing is picked: every bare door (`execute`, `getFlow`, `toggleFlow` and the rest) refuses a two-holder name with 409 naming both. A trigger refuses a shared slot until PR-2. So no flow that is dormant today fires from a trigger after this PR; it can be reached only by an exact `(package, name)` address. This is the arming my carry-in 1 asked for, and it is declared as `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.
  - **The Q4 condition** is met and pinned (ablation A6). A package-less disable row on P1:F binds to P1 when P2:F arrives, and the bound row survives a restart, so P1:F stays off.
  - **R9 credentials.** An insert for a two-holder name carries no package, so it serves neither slot. That is fail-closed until PR-2.
- **Red line 2, never guess: holds.** Precedence picks one winner per package. An environment body over a two-holder name overlays neither, logs one warning naming both, and is not armed.
- **Red line 3, independently releasable: holds.** A name with one holder keeps every key, log line and answer, byte for byte. Install still refuses a second holder. The forced rewrite of the #31754 describe is named in the PR body.

**Carried to PR-2 / PR-3:**
- When the triggers bind per slot in PR-2, that changeset must state that a sealed-clash pair's triggers **start firing**. That is the visible half of this widening.
- The S4 report lists sealed-clash flows and Q4 overlays (PR-3), so an operator sees them before upgrading.
- PR-3's switch keeps same-namespace co-owners refused (`bareNameHoldersMeet`).

epic:#31527#1 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzj7TEH65FDimZdn1H3

> **Amended (see 6764658726 on #31696):** the PASS below is withdrawn on red lines 1/2 for the cold-boot bind seat 1 found (M2 in 6764624467): a package-less disable row bound during the `kernel:ready` rehydrate goes to whichever package registers first. The superseding PR gets a fresh epic read.

~~**Epic delta read of #32091 (#31696 PR-1, `Part of #31696`), 77fa2e35 → e714e9b9: PASS on the three red lines.**~~ Contract review and ACCEPT are seat 1's. I read the commit, its changeset and the new pin names. I did not run anything.

- **Red line 1, never loosen: holds, and the delta is stricter than the PASS it amends.**
  - **A package-less disable row first read under two holders** used to give Q4's "overlay neither, both arm". Now it keeps every holder that has no row of its own off, with one warning, and it is never bound later, even if the name drops to one holder and comes back. That is fail-closed. It is the direction of open item 1 in 6761813588 (a package-less row under two holders is refused, never guessed). The operator's way out is `toggleFlowSlot`, which writes that package's own row.
  - **The bind of a one-holder row** (the condition in 6760226691) is now an awaited write. The second holder stays off until the write lands, and a failed write keeps both off and says why. All three states are pinned.
  - **An environment body over a two-holder name** overlays neither. That is not a loosening, because `flow` is Regime C (ADR-0126 §2/§3, the header of `flow-precedence.ts`): a stored row over a held name is shadowed and never dispatches, even with one holder. A customization of a packaged flow reaches the engine only through the disable switch, which is now bound per package, or a declared `.custom` override, which is judged on its stored binding. So no customization that is in force today is dropped.
- **Red line 2, never guess: holds.** The flow ledger is addressed by `(package, name)`. A write for one package never re-attributes another package's row. `adoptPackageless` is passed only for the name's one holder (D8), never for a two-holder name. A paused run, an http secret and a screen's progress go by the run's own slot, and a run stamps its package before any await. A bare door reads a `PACKAGE/NAME` spelling as a flow it does not hold.
- **Red line 3, independently releasable: holds, with the narrowings declared.** Every type other than flow keeps `'name'` addressing, and its one row per name is re-attributed as before (pinned). The two narrowings are declared as `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with the ADR-0087 marker. One is a rolling upgrade across a sealed clash: an old replica fails the run as unresumable and never runs it on the other package's flow. The other is a composition with no resolver: it used to arm one holder by precedence, which was a pick, and now refuses. First-party count is 0, and the remedies are stated. The `flow_package` value on one-holder rows is the additive nullable column, and earlier releases ignore it.

**Carried to PR-2 / PR-3** (added to the three in 6761675500):
1. The S4 report (PR-3) lists the package-less disable rows that keep a two-holder name off. Otherwise an operator sees "both flows off" with only a log line to explain it.
2. **Mixed-version ledger read.** With `'package-and-name'`, a package can now get a row beside a row of the same name that another package left behind, where before that row would have been re-attributed. A replica on an earlier release reads the ledger by name and takes the first match. Before PR-3 flips the switch, show that an uninstall removes or rebinds the departing package's flow ledger rows, or pin what an earlier replica reads when two rows of one name exist. Not blocking for PR-1, because install still refuses a second holder.
3. PR-2's changeset states that a sealed-clash pair's triggers start firing, unless an ambiguous package-less disable row keeps them off.

Judged on the tree, not the PR body.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong:

1. **Sealed clash (two packages ship one flow name): "arming neither" becomes "each package's flow armed in its own slot".** Right. It is the widening carry-in 1 asks for, and nothing is picked: the slot key is `PACKAGE/NAME` only while a name is shared (`flow-slots.ts` `FlowSlotTable.add`/`remove`).
2. **Bare doors on a shared name refuse, naming every holder** (`getFlow`, `toggleFlow`, `unregisterFlow`, `withdrawFlow`, `getFlowVersionHistory`, `rollbackFlow` throw `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` 409; `execute` answers `success: false` with the same sentence; the credential source wrapper throws for a bare shared name). Right (`engine.ts` `bareFlowKey` :4981, `resolveFlowKey` :4952). With a resolver, a shared name resolves only to the holder the resolver reaches for the caller's package. Without one, it resolves only to the caller's own slot, and otherwise it refuses. No branch picks.
3. **A `PACKAGE/NAME` spelling at a bare door is "a flow it does not hold"** (`isSlotKeySpelling` / `unfiledFlowKey`). Right: a flow name cannot contain `/` (`ROUTER_ADDRESSABLE_NAME_PATTERN`), so main answered the same.
4. **A composition with no flow-name resolver: a shared name was armed by one-owner precedence (a pick) on main. Here it is refused at the bare doors and declined on triggers.** Right on design: it is the fail-closed obligation 6729233545 that carry-in 6760047493 orders. But it is a **narrowing** of an accept set main serves, and it is outside the card's declared narrowing. See ② and ③ (M1).
5. **Rolling upgrade across a sealed clash.** The changeset lists it as narrowing 1. On the tree this narrows nothing main accepts: main arms neither flow of a sealed-clash name, so no paused run of either can exist there. It is a new failure mode of the new capability, and the changeset is right to describe it. Calling it a narrowing over-declares it, which is harmless.
6. **Triggers decline a slot of a shared name, one warning per slot** (`engine.ts` :4034). Right: this is red line 3, and no flow that is dormant on main fires from a trigger.
7. **R8 `sys_automation_run.flow_package`**: stamped on paused and terminal rows, including one-holder names, and a run resumes by `(flow_name, flow_package)`. Right. The run stamps its package before its first await (`dag-traversal.ts`), so a key that moves while the run is in flight cannot misfile it. A row of a package that no longer holds the name maps to a key nothing files and fails closed. The one-holder stored bytes do change; the changeset declares it, and the PR body's "byte for byte" overstates it (N4).
8. **R9 reads**: for a shared slot the channel is asked by package; a row naming no package answers only while one package holds the name. Right. **R9 writes**: the write door and promote still read, update and delete by name across packages. Wrong (M3).
9. **Flow activation ledger addressed by `(package, name)`** (`@objectstack/core` `MetadataActivationStoreOptions.addressing`, `MetadataActivationWriteOptions.adoptPackageless`). Every other type keeps `'name'`. Right; red line 3 holds for the other types. For one holder, `toggleFlow` passes `adoptPackageless`, which reproduces main's re-attribution of the package-less row.
10. **A package-less disable row is bound durably to the incumbent when a second holder arrives.** Wrong in the only arrival PR-1 can reach (M2).
11. **A package-less disable row first read under two holders keeps every holder without its own row off, and is never bound later.** Right on red line 1. It changes the recorded Q4 A ("both packages' own bodies arm") after the epic's PASS (S1).
12. **An environment body over a shared name overlays neither and is not armed, with one warning** (`flow-precedence.ts` `resolveSlotPrecedence` :169). Right. A runtime row of a shipped name is already shadowed under one holder (package rank 1 over runtime rank 2), so this loosens nothing.
13. **`declinesStoredRow` judges a stored flow row against every shipper** (`protocol-lock-state.ts`). Right. One shipper gives the same answer as before, and the fix stops a declared override from being dropped by registration order.
14. **Listing faces** (`listFlows`, `getFlowRuntimeStates`) list one row per slot under the bare name; a shared slot's run log carries the slot key. Right per Q2 A, and declared, with the spec follow-up left to the seat.
15. **New public surface**: `qualifiedFlowKey`, `FlowSlot`, `executeSlot`, `getFlowSlot`, `getFlowSlots`, `flowSlotKey`, `toggleFlowSlot`, `withdrawFlowSlot`, `packagedFlowSlotOwner`, `getRunFlow`, `flowKeyOfRun`, `flowActivationBinds`, `FlowContender.holder`, `FlowPrecedenceWinner.holder`, `SuspendedRun.flowPackage`/`RunRecord.flowPackage`, the core activation-store types, and the widened `PackagedFlowSource`/`FlowCredentialSource`. All additive, and the Q5 names are as ruled. One gap: a third-party `FlowCredentialSource` that ignores the new `flowPackage` answers every package's rows for a shared slot. The changeset declares the `SuspendedRunStore` half of this and not this one (S3).

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/core`, with `Metadata-protocol: none`. Correct: nothing an author can write changes, because install still refuses a second flow holder until PR-3 flips `NAMESPACE_SCOPED_BARE_NAME_TYPES`. The claim's `added` measured `none`; the deviation is declared and accepted, and `added` rides PR-3.
- **`Clause-②:` — the two carriers contradict each other (M1).**
  - The committed changeset says `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `feat(automation)!:`, carries a **BREAKING** banner and an ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`).
  - The PR body still says `Narrowing: no` / `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, and the title has no `!`.
  - AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist 3) requires one declaration on both carriers. On the tree the changeset is the true one, because of ① item 4.
- The `(narrowing)` arm decides the face: `reviewFace` reads `yes (narrowing)` on any carrier as the narrowing face, which maps to `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. That is why this record is served at that tier and not at the brief's `TIER_DEFAULT` (see ③).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Served tier.**
  - The brief served `TIER_DEFAULT` on the PR body's `(widening)` line. The committed tree carries a changeset whose `Clause-②:` line has the `(narrowing)` arm.
  - `record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths` finds no schema or governed-path hit, refuses to decide without that line, and names it as decisive. `reviewFace` maps it to the narrowing face, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.
  - Rendered at that tier; the Scope floor is every non-prose path of the diff. Nothing was built, run or re-run: the template tool only classified the path list.
- **Epic PASS is stale.**
  - 6761675500 PASSed at `77fa2e35`. The round-2 commit `e714e9b9` landed after it and changes three things:
    - Q4 behaviour, from "both arm" to "both off" (S1);
    - the activation bind, which is now an awaited durable write with a hold-off;
    - the declared clause, which is now a narrowing (M1).
  - The card's acceptance line says a narrowing beyond the declared one goes to the maintainer (`needs-user-decision`) before landing. The no-resolver narrowing (① item 4) is beyond the card's declared namespace co-owner narrowing.
  - **Escalated:** the epic seat either records that its carry-in 6760047493 (citing 6729233545) is the authority for that narrowing, or the maintainer rules on it. A red-line re-read at the new head is owed either way.
- **Dev report is stale.** The newest os-dev-report (6761628406) pins `77fa2e35`. Its `dogfood_battery: n/a — no ! in the PR title and no (narrowing) arm` is falsified by the round-2 changeset. With a `(narrowing)` arm, the full dogfood battery is owed at the final head (os-dev.md; review-checklist "`!` 或 `(narrowing)`" ⇒ REWORK if missing), and so is a `Skills-docs:` line. `Dogfood Regression Gate` is skipped on `pull_request` runs by design, so the check-runs do not stand in for the battery.
- **Dev deviations** (6761628406):
  - (1) `Metadata-protocol: none` over the claim's `added`: accepted.
  - (2) metadata-protocol fix in scope: accepted, since one-shipper behaviour is unchanged (① item 13).
  - (3) draft relay: n/a.
  - (4) "the R9 writer fails closed": true for inserts only. Updates and deletes cross packages (M3).
- **Check-runs** on `e714e9b9`: 55 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed. These are the gate verdicts, and none is red.
- **Serial constraints:** `bare-name-one-holder.ts` is untouched (only PR-3 may edit it). Line budget is 2,959 changed lines, under 3,000.
- **Carried, not owed here:** the Q3 re-arm pin, the schedule once-per-window pin, the inbound hook, the `/automation` doors and the S4 listing of Q4 overlays all belong to PR-2 or PR-3, as the epic carried them.

### ④ Design judgment

**M1 — must-fix — the clause declarations disagree, and the narrowing has not been routed.**
- Make the PR body and title agree with the committed changeset: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, drop `Narrowing: no`, add `!`, add `Skills-docs:`.
- Run the full dogfood battery at the final head and report it.
- Route the no-resolver narrowing per the card's acceptance line (③).
- Refresh the PR body's stale sentences:
  - "A package-less row overlays neither holder … (seat ruling Q4 A)", which the tree no longer does;
  - "byte for byte", which no longer holds for stored rows;
  - the public-name list, which is missing `getRunFlow`, `flowKeyOfRun`, `flowActivationBinds` and the core types.

**M2 — must-fix — the durable package-less bind is decided by boot order, which breaks red lines 1 and 2.**
- The mechanism:
  - `engine.ts` `placeFlowSlot` :4805 calls `bindPackagelessActivation` :4829 whenever a second package's slot arrives while one package slot is held.
  - It rewrites the ledger's package-less disable row as the incumbent's own row (`setActive({ name, packageId: holder, active: false }, { adoptPackageless: true })`).
  - `flow-activation-projection.ts` `canBindPackageless` :147 refuses only a row it has already read under two holders.
- On the tree, PR-1 reaches this bind only through a cold boot reassembling an existing clash. Install still refuses a new holder after the seal (`bare-name-one-holder.ts` "The cold boot").
- How the boot reassembles it:
  - `plugin.ts` pulls the registry at `start()` (:2444) and hydrates the ledger right after (:2495).
  - Installed packages are re-registered only at `kernel:ready` (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` `rehydrate`), where `syncFlowsFromProtocol` (:5692) registers the precedence winners in sorted package order (`flow-precedence.ts` :157).
- So for two installed packages that both ship `f`, with a package-less disable row:
  - the hydrate reads the row while no slot exists;
  - at `kernel:ready` the alphabetically first package becomes the "incumbent";
  - the second package's arrival binds the row to it durably, and the second package's flow arms.
- The same happens for a code package P1 plus an installed P2: the row binds to P1 because P1 was pulled at `start()`.
- In both cases the holder is chosen by arrival or sort order. The projection's own docblock calls that a pick ("a pick decided by arrival order"). The epic's condition (6760226691) allows a bind only at "the install of the second holder … one holder at that moment, so nothing is guessed", and no install happens here. Being durable, the guess outlives PR-1: once PR-2 binds triggers per slot, P2's trigger fires despite a row that may have been P2's switch.
- The red-line test (`flow-slots-per-package.test.ts` :326) pins the hydrate-then-second-arrival order as correct. The "first read under two holders" test (:359) registers both holders before the hydrate. Neither covers the `kernel:ready` rehydrate order.
- Fix: in PR-1, never bind during boot convergence. A package-less disable row over a name that becomes shared before the registry seal (`kernel:bootstrapped`) reads as "first read under two holders" and fails closed, both off with one warning, as round 2 already does in the other order. Leave the bind for a genuine post-seal install, which first exists in PR-3; the epic allowed "PR-1 or PR-3". Pin both installed-package boot orders.

**M3 — must-fix — the R9 write door and promote cross packages.**
- `flow-credential-channel.ts` `store()` :376 reads `readRows(engine, args.name, args.state)` (:386) with no package. Rows are collapsed by position, so one package's row stands for that position.
- For an existing position it **updates that row's secret**: a save under a shared name can overwrite the other package's stamped row.
- It then **deletes every row at a position the saved body no longer carries** (:437), including the other package's rows.
